covers: Indeterminate purpose: the RoPA entry never states the collection legal basis
title: Occupational health records for labour inspections

F-R1.quote: To check that employers in hazardous sectors arrange the periodic medical examinations their workers are required to have.

F-R2.quote: PDPL Article 15(3): disclosure requested by a public entity to implement another law, namely the Labour Law.

F-R3.quote: Protecting the health and safety of workers in hazardous sectors, a function given to the Ministry by the Labour Law.

F-R4.quote: Worker name, national ID number, employer establishment number, date of the last periodic medical examination.
items: date of the last periodic medical examination

F-R5.quote: Kept for two years after the related inspection is closed, then destroyed.

F-R6.quote: Requested by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development from the Ministry of Health.

F-P1.quote: Ministry of Health, Data Management Office, privacy@moh.example

F-P2.quote: Recording the periodic occupational medical examinations of workers in hazardous sectors and their results, and reporting examination dates to labour inspection authorities.

F-P4.quote: Worker name, national ID number, employer establishment number, date and result of each periodic medical examination.
items: date and result of each periodic medical examination

F-P5.quote: Workers in hazardous sectors who undergo periodic occupational medical examinations.

F-P6.quote: The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development, for labour inspections; other government entities where a law requires disclosure.

F-P7.quote: No transfer or disclosure outside the Kingdom.

F-P8.quote: Examination records are kept for fifteen years after the worker's last examination.
